title: Queue admission gates with plan nudging and graceful deprioritization
creator: Ayesha Patel
description: Goal: Implement an admission controller for per-tenant request admission that balances free/paid/enterprise lanes using credit-aware scoring and a soft-deprioritization path. The controller must: 1) allocate a short-lived admission score per request using available credits, plan entitlements, and recent latency/error signals; 2) support graceful deprioritization (soft demotion to cheaper model variants or lower-priority queues) rather than hard rejections for improved UX; 3) expose plan nudging hooks (rate-limited upgrade prompts surfaced in responses or analytics) and instrumentation for conversion experiments; 4) play nicely with region selection and model-variant fallback so we avoid cross-region thrash and uncontrolled spin-ups of expensive pools.
acceptance_criteria: Admission controller calculates an admission_score (0-100) for each request within 5ms median overhead under production load simulation
Requests with score < 30 are routed to a soft-deprioritized path (cheaper quantized variant or background lane) instead of immediate 429s
Quota deduction and replenishment logic prevents starvation: short bursts allowed using a borrow window and payback policy
Telemetry surfaces per-tenant admission_score distribution, demotion rate, and uplift from plan nudges
A staged rollout behind feature flag that can be toggled per-org and per-region without downtime
design_notes: Admission scoring inputs: tenant_credits_remaining, rolling_token_consumption(1h), recent_p90_latency(region), SLA_tier_weight, active_model_cost(weighted), emergency_override
Score composition strategy: linear blend with configurable weights and an exponential decay on historical debt to prefer recent behaviour

Soft-demotion options: (A) downgrade to quantized sibling model (same capability band), (B) route to background/predictive lane with lower priority and caching, (C) if model-variant unavailable, route to cross-region low-cost replica if latency budget allows
Plan nudging: attach a compact hint header and track nudges_sent per-org to avoid spam; experiment via console opt-in
Safety: fallback to hard rejection only if admission_score < 5 or request would breach critical safety quotas (billing or legal holds)
implementation_notes: Admission controller will live in gateway proxy as a lightweight filter to avoid extra RPC hops
Use existing credit ledger (ENG-62345) for authoritative balances; add a cache with TTL 2s for hot tenants
Introduce Borrow Window token bucket: allows 1 extra burst per 10s scaled by plan tier; payback enforced by higher future cost multiplier
Expose feature flags via rollout service and support per-org override for Dedicated customers
New metrics: admission_score_histogram, demotion_count, demotion_reason, nudges_sent, borrow_window_uses
testing_plan: Unit tests for scoring math and edge cases (negative credits, clock skew)
Load tests with synthetic tenants across tiers to validate controller overhead and demotion rates
Chaos scenarios: region outage to validate cross-region fallback path does not route into expensive pools
Canary rollout to 5% of free-tier orgs and 1% of paid-tier orgs, monitor errors and latency for 48h
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Internal QA and perf benchmarking in staging
Phase 2: Canary to selected tenants + runbook for immediate disable
Phase 3: Gradual ramp with telemetry thresholds to auto-pause rollout
Phase 4: Open to all tenants and enable plan nudging experiments
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: mis-calibrated scores cause unexpected demotions and customer complaints -> Mitigation: conservative defaults + telemetry + quick rollback flag
Risk: cross-region fallbacks spike egress or expensive GPUs -> Mitigation: per-region budget caps and cost-aware routing policy
Risk: feature inadvertently bypasses Dedicated isolation -> Mitigation: enforced per-deployment policy check and automated integration test
Risk: upgrade prompts create UX friction -> Mitigation: throttle nudges and A/B test content and placement
